Options: Functional lumen imaging probe distensibility study

before: **KEY:** Laparoscopic Heller myotomy
The adequate primary-position study establishes absent peristalsis with impaired junction relaxation. Myotomy is an established junction-directed treatment.
Oral omeprazole therapy
Reflux-directed acid suppression does not treat the demonstrated junction-relaxation and body-motility problem. A normal upright pressure does not erase the adequate primary-series findings.
Oral isosorbide dinitrate therapy

Pharmacological junction relaxation is a less effective palliative approach, rather than the preferred durable treatment for a routine procedural candidate. It can have a role when definitive options are unsuitable.
after: **KEY:** Endoscopic ultrasound with wall sampling

The motor pattern does not exclude a secondary junction process. Eccentric wall thickening and resistance despite unrevealing mucosal samples make deeper wall assessment the priority among these procedures.
Functional lumen imaging probe distensibility study
This can complement equivocal motor assessment, but another distensibility measurement does not establish the cause of the focal wall abnormality.
Timed barium esophagram with a tablet
This can characterize bolus emptying, but the new wall finding requires etiologic tissue assessment rather than another measure of impaired passage.

before: **KEY:** Separated single-water-swallow pressure series
The existing sequences test inhibition and recovery; they do not supply a separated baseline series for body classification.

Preserved post-swallow reserve with preserved junction relaxation

before: **KEY:** Reduced contraction reserve; obtain a timed barium esophagram
The reduced recovery integral concerns reserve, not proof of a junction obstruction. Assess actual emptying before selecting junction-disrupting treatment.
Reduced contraction reserve; arrange pneumatic junction dilation
The reserve finding does not itself establish an outflow lesion that would justify dilation.
Preserved contraction reserve; obtain a timed barium esophagram
An emptying assessment is reasonable, but the stated recovery integrals do not demonstrate augmentation.
Preserved contraction reserve; arrange pneumatic junction dilation
This both overcalls augmentation and converts discomfort into an unsupported indication to disrupt the junction.
after: **KEY:** Reduced post-swallow reserve with preserved junction relaxation

The software-integrated recovery responses do not augment the baseline despite taller peaks. Baseline propagation and the liquid-load relaxation observations do not establish absent body contractility or impaired junction relaxation.
Preserved post-swallow reserve with preserved junction relaxation
The junction component fits, but peak height is not the integrated contractile response. The measured recovery integrals do not demonstrate augmentation.
Absent esophageal body contractility with impaired junction relaxation

This mistakes the quiet clustered-swallow phase for baseline failure and the presence of dysphagia for junction obstruction. Traveling baseline waves and the recorded relaxation behavior contradict those claims.

before: **KEY:** Refer for elective inguinal hernia repair
The limiting stock task reproduces the protrusion-associated episode. The coexisting hip changes do not establish the cause of that particular limitation.
Continue inguinal hernia surveillance with graded activity
This is reasonable for a minimally symptomatic inguinal hernia, but the current full-load work task is limited by the protrusion-associated event.
Refer for hip-directed physiotherapy
This addresses a real separate symptom, but the observed stock-lifting episode is localized to the protrusion rather than the reproduced joint-line ache.

The old report describes an anterior mesh plane. A posterior preperitoneal approach is the offered route that avoids re-entering that operated plane for a symptomatic recurrence.

Changing to a tissue repair does not change the fact that this is another anterior-plane operation after the recorded anterior mesh repair.

title: Use the biochemical branch despite a competing incidental image
keyOrderNotice: key shown first for review only; runtime choices randomized
reviewDisplayNote: Before is the exact round-two version assessed by independent review two; after is the final round-three draft. Jamie Taylor substitutes for patientName. No clinical approval or release is implied.

before.Presentation: Jamie Taylor, a 44-year-old woman, attends the clinic after CT performed for an unrelated complaint shows a 2.3-cm adrenal nodule.
before.Current update: Post-test serum cortisol remains above this laboratory’s suppression decision limit on repeated overnight dexamethasone studies.
before.Task: Which study should guide the next etiologic step in Jamie Taylor’s cortisol evaluation?

after.Presentation: Jamie Taylor, a 44-year-old woman, attends the clinic after CT performed for an unrelated complaint shows a 2.3-cm adrenal nodule.
after.Current update: The nodule was seen on an abdominal CT acquired in the portal venous phase. Late-night salivary cortisol and urine free-cortisol results exceed their laboratory decision limits on repeated assessment. Medication review records no oral, inhaled, injected or topical glucocorticoid use. Basal plasma ACTH is below the laboratory reporting limit on repeat sampling. A previous headache MRI also describes a small pituitary focus of lower enhancement.
after.Task: Which imaging study should be prioritized to investigate the source of Jamie Taylor’s cortisol findings?

before: **KEY:** Basal plasma corticotropin measurement
ACTH classifies the etiologic branch after biochemical cortisol assessment. An adrenal nodule does not establish that it is the cortisol source.
High-dose dexamethasone suppression study
A specialized suppression comparison does not replace establishing the basal ACTH branch first.
Corticotropin-releasing hormone stimulation study
A stimulation/localization pathway should not be selected from the incidental anatomical finding before basal ACTH classification.
after: **KEY:** Noncontrast adrenal CT

The repeated biochemical pattern supports an ACTH-independent branch, so the incidental pituitary focus does not redirect the evaluation. The existing contrast-only abdominal acquisition has not supplied the unenhanced adrenal assessment.
Dedicated pituitary MRI
The small focus is an anchoring temptation. Pituitary localization belongs to an ACTH-dependent evaluation; repeatedly suppressed ACTH does not support making that focus the source here.
Contrast-enhanced chest CT

A search for an ectopic ACTH source can be relevant in an ACTH-dependent pathway. The supplied hormone pattern instead directs adrenal evaluation; neither the incidental adrenal size nor the pituitary image substitutes for that classification.

inference: Interpret the independently abnormal cortisol findings and repeatedly suppressed ACTH as an adrenal-directed, rather than ACTH-dependent, evaluation. Then: Use that branch and the actual prior CT acquisition to choose the named adrenal study over targeting an incidental pituitary focus or an ectopic ACTH source.
focus: Use a supported cortisol/ACTH pattern to choose adrenal imaging despite an incidental pituitary focus, rather than recall the next basal assay after suppression testing.
whatChanged: Replaced recall of the next basal measurement with interpretation of measured hormones before choosing among three named imaging targets. Added a plausible competing incidental image, raw prior-CT acquisition facts and specific exposure history. The lead-in is one complete imaging task, with no etiologic-stage cue or competing hormonal screens.
clinicalMeaning: The score changes from obtaining basal ACTH to applying an already measured hormone pattern to the anatomical investigation. Preserve the initial-screen and etiologic-assay constructs and their histories.
sourceDecision: Offline mapping to recorded Endocrine Society/Endotext and ESE/AAES guidance. The ACTH source-localization fact has one directly recorded supporting reference; exact endocrine application and imaging wording require clinician review. No numerical cortisol/ACTH threshold, dose, washout, operation indication or ACTH-dependent localization hierarchy is introduced.
